correction_summary: The two 40M XRP Whale Alert transfers are only a subset of a broader November 2 redistribution. Ledger-derived reporting describes nine bulk transfers totaling approximately 233.455M XRP to six new addresses, plus seven 1,000-XRP test payments. Do not describe the two 40M transfers as the full movement or infer that the recipient addresses belong to the attacker or Binance.

source_capture.method: Public web-rendered source extraction; transaction identifiers and ledger snapshot references retained
limitations: No raw HTTP byte capture or immutable source receipt was created in this run.
The November 2 full recipient set is based on independent secondary ledger reconstructions; direct node RPC responses were not captured by this run.
Beneficial ownership of the six bulk recipient accounts is unresolved.

sources.supports: Five hot wallets sent 233.46M XRP to one attacker-controlled address between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC on October 29; the attack involved access to wallet signing infrastructure.
233.46M XRP across five Binance wallets; 88.5M RLUSD on Ethereum; 40.5M RLUSD frozen by Ripple; assessment that signing infrastructure was compromised.
Five XRPL transaction CTIDs and amounts; initial attacker account; failed retries; no outgoing movement as of its October 30 cutoff; separate 51.17M RLUSD movement on XRPL.

Direct XRPL account transaction and account state queries through ledger 108064685; 16 source-account outgoing transactions, nine bulk transfers to six recipients, seven test payments, and no recipient outflows as of the stated cutoff.
Bithomp-based reconstruction of nine large transfers to six recipients and no later recipient outflows at its observation time.
One 40M XRP transfer from rK21t6... to rhXt...; provider labels both addresses Binance Hack 2026.
Interprets the final 80M movement as Binance sweeping funds to internal wallets; this is not a first-party Binance attribution of the six recipients.
Zero-knowledge Proof of Reserves for the October 31 00:00 UTC snapshot covering ten assets including XRP and RLUSD; users can verify 1:1 balance inclusion.
Binance reports 98% replenishment, 100%+ funds set aside, a 44-token November 4 snapshot, and proof expected in 50-60 hours.
Phased withdrawal restoration; the XRP network entry names RLUSD as the asset, while the BSC list separately includes XRP.
Native XRP cannot be frozen; issued trust-line tokens can have issuer freeze controls; custodial exchanges can freeze assets they custody.

claims.conclusion: The XRP Ledger was the first chain hit in the multi-chain incident. The valid signed transfers indicate compromise of Binance's signing path, not an XRPL consensus exploit.

limitations: The reported recipient total plus source residual exceeds the initial 233,461,943.1 XRP by 0.59905 XRP; no explanation is assigned.
No outgoing or DEX offer was observed through ledger 108064685; later activity is not covered.
No destination is identified as an exchange. This does not exclude OTC, bridge activity or later sales.

claims.timestamp_mapping_conflict: The Crypto Basic associates its 03:55:31 UTC statement with the link that resolves to hash 3AAA, but Whale Alert's transaction page for 3AAA reports 03:56:21 UTC. The second hash DC8D was not independently opened. Q-Eternal places the full distribution within 03:52-04:00 UTC.
limitations: 80M is not the total November 2 movement; it is two of nine bulk transfers.

hypotheses.support: Q-Eternal describes the source as the attacker account and records six newly created recipients.
hypotheses.limitation: Recipient names and beneficial owners are unknown; no outgoing transfers or DEX offers were observed at the snapshot.

hypotheses.support: Coinotag and U.Today describe the final 80M as Binance moving funds to internal wallets.
hypotheses.limitation: No first-party Binance statement identifies the six recipient addresses as Binance-controlled; the full ledger reconstruction describes the entire 233.46M distribution.

hypotheses.support: Recipient accounts are newly created and unlabelled.

claims.conclusion: Do not label the six recipients as attacker-owned or Binance-owned.

limitations: This is ERC-20 RLUSD on Ethereum, not native XRP or the separate XRPL RLUSD movement.

hypotheses: Binance moved remaining RLUSD to safety
limitations: XRPLWin says the purpose was unclear and funds had not moved by its October 30 cutoff. Do not conflate with Ethereum's 88.5M RLUSD.

claims.claim: Native XRP has no issuer and cannot be frozen or clawed back by Ripple or another XRPL participant. Issuer freeze controls apply to issued tokens such as RLUSD. Custodial exchanges can freeze assets held in their own custody.

limitations: This is proof of user-balance inclusion for ten assets at a dated snapshot; it is not proof that stolen XRP was recovered or purchased on the market.
The 98% is aggregate affected-asset replenishment, not an XRP-specific flow. The new 44-token proof was pending at publication.
This is the XRP network with RLUSD as the asset, not a claim that native XRP withdrawals on XRPL resumed at that time.

competing_hypotheses.description: The controller of the hack-linked source account distributed the stolen XRP to six newly created addresses.
supporting: Ledger-derived reconstruction records nine bulk transfers and six recipients.
The source address is the same one initially funded by five Binance hot wallets.
disconfirming_or_missing: No recipient account names or destination tags.
No outgoing or DEX offer at the November 2 snapshot.

competing_hypotheses.description: Binance regained control and moved the remaining stolen XRP into new internal custody wallets.
supporting: Coinotag and U.Today interpret the final 80M as an internal Binance sweep.
Binance was restoring affected assets and had resumed phased withdrawals.
disconfirming_or_missing: No official Binance statement identifies the six recipient addresses as internal.
The full ledger reconstruction covers 233.46M, not only the final 80M.
Recipient names and tags are absent.

competing_hypotheses.description: A third party or intermediary controls some recipient addresses.

market_implications.conditional_supply_overhang: Only if a recipient later sends XRP to exchange deposit infrastructure, XRPL DEX/AMM, bridges or OTC sell-side liquidity.
market_implications.recovery_distinction: Binance's customer-balance backing and PoR proof are distinct from recovery or return of the stolen XRP.
market_implications.price_causation: No causal price effect is established.

data_quality.reason_model_ineligible: The full ledger transaction set was not directly retrieved in this run; recipient ownership is unresolved; a 0.59905 XRP balance reconciliation gap remains; and raw source bytes were not retained.
